public_rationale: On August 7, 2025, OpenAI reported factual-error improvements on prompts representative of ChatGPT traffic, with web search enabled: GPT-5 responses were about 45% less likely to contain a factual error than GPT-4o responses, and GPT-5 with thinking about 80% less likely than o3 [e6]. Epoch AI’s analysis, published August 29, said selected benchmark results suggested a large advance from GPT-4 to GPT-5; it cautioned that gains across successive generations were not directly comparable [e7]. The reported factuality gains in the August 1–18 target window, supplemented by Epoch’s later analysis of the release, contradict “hit a wall” understood as stalled meaningful progress [e6] [e7].
limitations: The factuality figures are company-reported; Epoch’s analysis does not independently verify them [e6] [e7].
The evaluations do not establish complete solutions to reasoning, hallucinations, basic errors and factuality, or improvement on every task [e6] [e7].
The evidence does not isolate the training changes responsible for the gains, so it cannot conclusively settle the “new technique” qualification [e6] [e7].
The assessment uses the contract’s interpretation of “hit a wall” as stalled meaningful progress.
